lark_e15_entry.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_entry.text: On Day Ninety Five, the clinician found that Lin still shortened the last part of her left step. The swelling had fallen enough for her to mistake improvement for readiness. Crossing the lower room twice made the difference visible again. She had brought her ordinary shoes and put them on without help, then found herself looking for the stool before the second turn. The clinician did not ask whether she could endure more. She asked what the foot actually did when Lin stopped arranging each step for an observer. Its ordinary movement answered before her ambition could.

lark_e15_entry_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_entry_002.text: The current assessment cost five of the reserved care copper. Six had now been received, thirty spent, and ten remained for two later offered assessments. Lin accepted another protected interval through Day One Hundred Nine, followed by a current reassessment on the tenth morning after the hundredth. The plan retained ordinary gentle movement inside the presently accepted range. It did not allow leg reinforcement, a return to the gallery, or an attempt to complete the fifth pair by ignoring the ankle. The recovered shoulder still had its older limits beside the newer wound.

lark_e15_entry_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_entry_003.text: The crutch keeper extended the temporary hire for fifteen actual days at two copper. The first four copper hire had covered the initial interval through yesterday; it had not purchased the crutch forever. With the original six for the wrap, ordinary treatment materials and hire had now used twelve of twenty, leaving eight. Lin signed the current end date where she could find it before another busy morning. The wooden support was heavier than the elegant walking stick offered in a shop. It was also the thing the clinician had actually fitted to her present movement.

lark_e15_entry_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_entry_004.text: Qin brought the crutch downstairs without suggesting she should test it on the market stair. He had a newly accepted lower road load later that afternoon. The route went around the damaged freight bays and required more ordinary pulling than the old gallery movement. Its carrier price had risen, but his completed hours would still have to earn the offered fee before he could buy supper with it. Lin watched him adjust the shoulder pad on the empty harness. He did not resemble a man compensated by the fact that another household had lost more.

lark_e15_entry_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_entry_005.text: The clinic's patient chair stood inside the lower receiving room today. Nobody asked Lin to climb to an inquiry that had already finished. Ke Lan's planned departure or extension depended on the actual support arrangement the family had accepted. The ordinary kitchen keeper had the meal dates, the licensed petition receiver had any paid dispatch, and the association desk had its own later review. Lin put the relevant receipt where the keeper could read it without turning a sister's company into proof that every offered form of help had happened. Their plans had different mornings.

lark_e15_entry_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_entry_006.text: Before the family receiving, she completed her own small dispatch. The licensed ordinary carrier accepted the sealed letter to her mother at the lower desk, named the current route, and took one copper from Lin's personal purse. The letter described the ankle, the separate present care, and the fact that some people had been hurt worse. It did not ask her mother to imagine a cure arriving through affectionate concern. Lin kept the carrier's actual receiving until its next report. The earlier unsealed page had become one sent account rather than an indefinitely postponed answer.

lark_e15_entry_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_entry_007.text: The carrier did not promise a reply by an examination date. Roads and household evenings belonged to ordinary schedules. Lin asked when a current delivery report would be offered and accepted that narrower answer. Across the room, a boy was waiting with a basket of empty medicine jars for the provider who owned them. He kept inventing ways to arrange their different mouths in rows. His mother told him to keep the glass below his chin. The ordinary interruption made Lin smile. An actual letter could leave her hands without giving her command over its whole journey.

lark_e15_entry_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_entry_008.text: Ke Wen's note had asked for no public reading of the intimate parts of his treatment. The keeper retained the permission on the work summary and left the rest with the patient receiver. A market visitor arrived with a proposal to sell his story as a great sacrifice. Shan Fang asked which offered account gave her the right. The visitor said everyone already knew enough. Knowing that a man had lost a lower arm was not ownership of what he felt afterward. The proposal left the room without its promised material or an endorsement borrowed from the wound.

lark_e15_family_gate.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_family_gate.text: The keeper read the accepted support receiving before preparing the sister's current dates. A paid petition left her original return today intact. A gift of six served meals extended the visit through the hundredth day and moved her own return to the following morning. The later community review left today's return intact as well. The family would perform the arrangement it had actually accepted, with no meal or journey inserted merely because another possible gift would have sounded comforting.

lark_e15_petition_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_petition_001.text: Ke Lan's original carriage took her down on Day Ninety Five. Lin watched only its lower receiving, where the sister handed the fare she had kept and checked that the driver's destination matched the booking. The clinic could send current news through the contact she had actually supplied. Her brother remained under the qualified provider's accepted care, with no claim that a departing relative had abandoned that work. Ke Lan put a little wrapped winter herb in his permitted cupboard before leaving. Its familiar smell was company he could receive without pretending it treated the wound.

lark_e15_petition_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_petition_002.text: She thanked Lin for the application and said she wished a paper could keep someone in a chair another evening. Lin did not answer that the larger possible grant would certainly prove better. The received dispatch had purchased a timely place in a process, not its answer. The lower room lost the sister's actual evening company today. The road took her back to a household whose other work could not wait forever, even while a guide's future had been cut into an unfamiliar shape. Their goodbye had more than one practical reason.

lark_e15_petition_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_petition_003.text: On Day Ninety Seven, the district receiving report came back through its authorized outward loop. The bounded petition had reached the docket in time. A competent clerk would examine the submitted work injury scope against the present support conditions; further information, if needed, would travel through the guide's permitted receiver. Lin saw the actual stamp and returned the report to Ke Wen's keeper. It was not an approval or twenty four copper already waiting in a pocket. The next offered decision report would come after the district's current review, with ordinary road days added.

lark_e15_petition_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_petition_004.text: Ke Wen asked the keeper to show him which condition might fail. The living support was offered for present reduced earning capacity from an accepted current work injury. His qualified operation had a separate paid source, so it was not claimed again as an unpaid bill. Future adaptation was not required to have succeeded before the application could be considered. Lin heard the clerk's permitted readback from the doorway. The guide wanted a process he could understand, not a compassionate exception too vague to know whether it was still being discussed.

lark_e15_petition_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_petition_005.text: By the hundredth evening, the sister's chair had been folded beside the lower wall. No additional visiting meals had been bought by Lin or charged invisibly to the provider. Ke Wen asked Shan Fang to take home a mending question for his sister when she next wrote. It concerned the looseness of the old flute cloth, which he wanted left ordinary rather than made ceremonial. The district had not answered yet. A timely petition could coexist with an empty chair and a small household question still needing somebody's consented attention.

lark_e15_food_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_food_001.text: The first additional meal was served to Ke Lan on Day Ninety Five, and Lin paid its one copper after the kitchen receiver named it completed. It was bean broth with the ordinary portion of grain, not a ceremonial feast. Ke Lan ate beside her brother after checking that his present treatment allowed company at that hour. She had already paid her own room within the extended visit she could afford. The gift bought this meal and the five later dates. The kitchen did not turn gratitude into a reason to bill Lin for another week.

lark_e15_food_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_food_002.text: Ke Lan spent the next afternoon arguing gently with her brother over the proper beginning of their father's tune. He remembered the loading rhythm first; she remembered a slower household phrase their mother had sung before the freight bell sounded. Neither account could make his absent hand return to the second set of flute holes. They disagreed without needing that disagreement to be a lesson in courage. Lin heard them while the permitted door was open and later asked which beginning she should try to remember. They told her to remember both until she could actually hear the difference.

lark_e15_food_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_food_003.text: The second and third additional meals were received on Days Ninety Six and Ninety Seven. Lin paid one copper after each, leaving three of her reserved six. The provider recorded the ordinary served dates beside the actual room arrangement rather than charging through a cousin's promise. Ke Lan used one evening to write a family letter with her brother's permitted words. She would carry it when she left. The continued company mattered in the small corrections he could make aloud before a sentence became the distant family's whole picture of his days.

lark_e15_food_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_food_004.text: The fourth and fifth meals followed on Days Ninety Eight and Ninety Nine, with two more actual copper paid by Lin. Ke Lan brought the old double flute in its checked cloth. Her brother asked to see it, touched the smooth place his right hand knew, and then put it away himself. He did not perform an improvised miracle for the visitor's benefit. The sister asked whether he wanted it left nearby or taken home. He wanted it in the cupboard where he could ask for it again without a household deciding every morning whether he was ready.

lark_e15_food_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_food_005.text: On Day One Hundred, the sixth received meal used the last reserved copper. The extra visit had happened, and its gift ended at the named scope. Ke Lan's rebooked carriage received her own fare the following morning. The current district docket had closed without Lin's paid petition; the six copper had bought company rather than a timely application. At the lower departure, the sister said the evenings had let them speak about ordinary things again. Lin could accept that result without calling the missed possible living grant imaginary or promising another funded visit.

lark_e15_wait_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_wait_001.text: Ke Lan left under her original Day Ninety Five carriage booking. Lin accompanied the actual lower receiving inside her ordinary movement limit and returned to the supported chair before the cart moved out of sight. The sister had kept her fare and supplied the clinic's permitted family contact. There was no new visiting meal charge to settle. Ke Wen's current care continued through the received guides' fund, while the later community review sat on the association's offered agenda. Keeping six personal copper had not kept the family together for six more evenings.

lark_e15_wait_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_wait_002.text: The review receiver sent the guide a plain question about possible seated work he might actually want. It did not ask him to prove he was cheerful enough for charity. A future tally scope would require current readiness, a task he could handle with the hand he had, accepted limits and an actual client willing to pay. Ke Wen wrote that he could discuss such a question after the next ordinary wound check. He would not promise it now to make the association's record look useful before any new work had been offered.

lark_e15_wait_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_wait_003.text: Lin kept the six copper in her own purse. She had expected that restraint to feel simpler once the sister's carriage departed. Instead she could hear the absent evening voices through the room where they had been. Shan Fang said a preserved road purse was still a concrete choice, with an ordinary future use. She did not call it a disguised gift to the guide. Lin was grateful for the refusal to make every defended personal need sound generous. The association had accepted correspondence; she had accepted a smaller personal cost.

lark_e15_wait_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_wait_004.text: On Day Ninety Eight, the receiver confirmed the community discussion for the one hundred twelfth morning. Its ordinary desk arrangement covered placing the bounded work account and notifying its permitted receivers. No new wage, grant or material budget had yet been approved. Lin took the actual notice to the lower cupboard and left it where the guide could ask for it. The appointment supplied something she had chosen: a later opportunity to be heard. It also named the days during which the family would still wait without a paid living support.

lark_e15_wait_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_wait_005.text: Ke Wen's answer asked for any eventual work offer to describe its ordinary hours before its comforting purpose. He knew a small task could become an unending public proof that he remained useful. The receiver accepted that question for the actual agenda. The present district docket stayed missed, and nobody dated the community appointment backward to hide it. Lin watched the guide's right hand fold the notice awkwardly at its narrow edge. She wanted to help with the fold, then waited until he asked for the lower corner held. He had asked for one assistance, not a new keeper.

lark_e15_common_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_common_001.text: By Day One Hundred Two, the lower room had become quieter in the ordinary pattern of received departures. Lin could describe her own protected dates without assuming the guide's family had shared every one. Ke Wen's clinic room remained one of the six admitted places under its separate patient agreement. The accepted twenty eight copper operation and immediate care scope had included that bed and its ordinary patient meals through the planned Day One Hundred Ten review. It bought a finite stay. It had not made the clinic a permanent home or paid a visiting sister.

lark_e15_common_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_common_002.text: The guides' receiver showed the separate ongoing care line to Ke Wen before its next use. Two current ordinary wound followups, on Days Ninety Five and One Hundred Three, had been accepted at six copper each from the thirty two remaining after the initial scope. The first had actually occurred; the second still needed its present work. Twenty would remain after both were received. The terms included the named examination and dressing, not a restored hand or every future expense. Lin's own care eighty stayed in its different employment account, without another patient's costs slipped into it.

lark_e15_common_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_common_003.text: Ke Wen wanted his future home arrangements discussed before the finite clinic stay ended. His own lower lane house had passed its current ordinary building check after the slope event, but an intact door was not a complete plan for entering with a changed body. Zhou Min offered an actual daylight route check within her new guide appointment before a return was accepted. It would name the approach, ordinary assistance if needed, and receiving household contact. Ke Wen agreed to hear it. He would not be sent home merely because a chart needed its bed counted empty.

lark_e15_common_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_common_004.text: The keeper brought him a shallow tray with three objects he had asked to compare: an ordinary cup, a low handled mug, and the smooth lidded jar that held his tea. The potter lent those samples for a short current grip comparison and would receive them back without sale. No one presented them as a gift he must admire. Ke Wen took the ordinary cup with his right hand and found its rim easy enough when empty. The lidded jar wanted another hand to steady its body. He put it down and asked for the mug next.

lark_e15_visit_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_visit_001.text: On the one hundred second afternoon, Ke Wen came to Lin's lower doorway in the supported chair under the clinic's accepted short visit. He held the empty mug and said its maker had apparently expected tea to be drunk rather than venerated. Lin laughed and asked whether that was enough reason to buy it. He said he was still testing the handle. His left sleeve remained closed over the permanent below elbow loss. The visit had not changed the wound's current care or given him a hand with which to hold the other side.

lark_e15_visit_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_visit_002.text: Lin held the sample tray at its accepted low position while he placed the mug down. She did not fasten a strap around him or propose a convenient mechanism before he described the difficulty. The handle's angle twisted his ordinary wrist at the last inch. They turned the tray instead and tried the empty movement again. It helped at that position, with no promise about carrying hot tea elsewhere. A modest successful turn could matter without becoming a story in which the guide's new life had already been solved by a clever student.

lark_e15_visit_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_visit_003.text: He asked whether the potter had spoken to somebody with only one usable hand before making the sample. Lin said she did not know. They sent that actual question with the permitted return rather than assume the shape proved an experience its maker might never have had. Ke Wen liked the mug enough to ask its offered price, then refused to decide before the ordinary full cup could be compared safely. Lin was glad he still wanted to argue with a pot. The argument belonged to him and did not require an audience to declare him brave.

lark_e15_visit_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_visit_004.text: The double flute stayed wrapped inside the guide's cupboard. Lin asked whether he wanted her to bring it during this visit. He said no today, with neither apology nor promise for tomorrow. He would first learn what small daily motions the hand he had could perform without turning the whole afternoon into fatigue. The permanent missing left lower arm was not an unfinished pair waiting to be opened. Lin could hear the difference most clearly when he refused the object she had hoped would make their conversation feel like the old daylight walk.

lark_e15_visit_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_visit_005.text: Qin Yi came to the doorway with Shan Fang after the permitted visit had nearly ended. The child had drawn the guide with his right hand holding a great bell rope. Her mother asked whether he wanted to receive that picture. Ke Wen said he would prefer a smaller rope whose bell he had actually used. Qin Yi looked offended by the revision, then asked how small. He used the empty mug's handle to show its ordinary scale. She went away with a concrete alteration instead of being praised for inventing an impossible version of his work.

lark_e15_visit_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_visit_006.text: Lin expected the guide to complain about the drawing once the child left. He said it had given him a reason to correct something that was not his body. He was tired of every conversation beginning with what he could no longer do. The ordinary smaller bell belonged to a childhood errand, with no professional gallery guide scope attached. He might teach its rhythm if he actually wanted to later. Today he wanted the clinic chair taken back before the visit tired him. Lin asked the attendant for that current receiving and did not argue for five more cheerful minutes.

lark_e15_market_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_market_001.text: The permitted sample return went through the potter's ordinary messenger. The maker answered that an older customer with a stiff left hand had corrected the first handle, and no customer with Ke Wen's present loss had yet tried it. He offered a safe full cup comparison after the guide's current care allowed it, with the normal price still three copper if the man eventually wanted to buy. The honest answer pleased Lin more than an invented history of perfect consideration. A useful object could have learned something already and still need this particular user's judgment.

lark_e15_market_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_market_002.text: Shan Fang took Qin Yi's revised drawing to the school within her own accepted lesson time. The children compared whether a picture's rope had enough room to move before its figure could actually pull it. The lesson concerned visible ordinary scale and did not make a patient's body public teaching stock. Shan had Ke Wen's permission for the smaller bell example, not the clinic visit or the details of his dressing. Lin heard the returned lesson account at supper and was invited to laugh at the disproportionate rope without laughing at the absent arm.

lark_e15_market_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_market_003.text: The lower market had resumed a fraction of its ordinary noise. A freight seller stood beside an empty upper gallery ticket board and offered lower road carriage instead. The new price took longer work seriously; customers still argued that the old movement ought to be cheap because they remembered it. Qin had accepted one qualified lower load at the offered current price and completed it on Day One Hundred Three. His pay belonged to that job's source and his own family. Lin could hear his tired laugh below the room without entering another wages line in her course.

lark_e15_market_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_market_004.text: The widow's dry stock had been checked under its own buyer's receiving. Some baskets had held; some had warped in the damp days. Lin asked the association receiver whether the public notice could list both rather than announce the market restored. The widow wanted the usable stock named clearly because she had bills to meet. She also wanted the failed liners marked so a customer would not take one home and call the next failure her secret. An honest notice could support present trade without making a damaged mountain look whole.

lark_e15_market_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_market_005.text: The former upper route seller complained that lower road prices would destroy his business. Zhou Min asked whether his stated cheap route included a currently accepted path. It did not. He said she was turning every ordinary question into a reason for delay. Lin heard the irritation from the low receiving desk and recognized a feeling she had carried into her fifth pair. A refusal to pretend a route worked could become personal in a room where somebody's next meal depended on it. The guide kept the current closure and asked which ordinary alternative he could actually offer.

lark_e15_market_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_market_006.text: Qin showed the seller the new harness pad and the time his received load had taken. The man had expected some of the extra distance to be covered by an ambitious cultivator volunteering a faster pull. Qin said his family could not buy supper with a task an unpaid stranger might happen to complete. The debate ended without universal agreement. Two customers accepted the lower carriage offer; another took his parcel home. Lin watched the three real answers separate. The market would have to learn its reduced capacity through ordinary refusals as well as received work.

lark_e15_care_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_care_001.text: The qualified work cover received its third accepted session on Day One Hundred One and its fourth on Day One Hundred Five. Each completed session cost five of the remaining ten care cover copper. All twenty had now bought actual replacement work while Lin could not perform her scheduled role. Those completed hours belonged to the substitute, whose own employer receiving paid them. Lin got no wage for the canceled personal shifts. Her twenty one completed shifts still meant eighty four received copper, with twenty four possible shifts left only if present recovery and actual offered work later allowed them.

lark_e15_care_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_care_002.text: The substitute asked Lin which public drawer held the corrected knot explanation. Lin answered from the lower room, then stopped herself before turning the question into an hour of unaccepted remote work. The receiver had asked for a location, not another performed shift on Lin's record. He thanked her and took the actual assignment back to the desk. She could be useful in a small ordinary way without billing herself for a day her ankle had canceled. The empty afternoon afterward made that distinction harder to like than it had been to state.

lark_e15_care_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_care_003.text: The protected movement exercises were dull enough for Lin to resent their precision. She placed the foot inside its current accepted range, shifted only the ordinary weight the clinician had allowed, and returned to the chair before the movement changed. No talisman received a useful fraction. No internal pair was tested. The exercise had a different object: making the presently injured body able to move ordinarily without teaching it to hide pain behind an effort. She could count its completed motions without trying to trade them for a cultivation result they had never promised.

lark_e15_care_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_care_004.text: On Day One Hundred Four, she tried to tidy the shelf standing up and found herself leaning on the right edge longer than she realized. The uneven stance pulled her recovering shoulder against the book she had meant to move easily. She sat down before the shelf was finished. Shan Fang arrived with the ordinary school notice and saw the one crooked volume. Lin expected another warning. Shan asked whether she wanted the volume lowered or left where it was. It was the kinder question because it allowed the unfinished shelf to remain merely unfinished.

lark_e15_care_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_care_005.text: Ke Wen's second accepted six copper followup had been received the previous morning, leaving twenty in his separate ongoing care fund. Its qualified wound judgment continued the actual care course and allowed the present limited chair visits. It did not restore the lost lower arm. The guide was learning how much fatigue followed an ordinary right hand task before agreeing to do it again. Lin could understand that caution without borrowing his more visible injury to explain her own ankle. Both bodies had actual present limits, with different work and different ordinary treatment.

lark_e15_care_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_care_006.text: The provider put a new lower stool near Lin's door after she requested it. It came from the room's own accepted furniture, not a purchase quietly charged to the eight remaining treatment copper. The old higher stool went back to its ordinary cupboard. Lin had wanted to ignore the awkward transfer because asking felt like another announcement of being hurt. Once the stool stood there, she found she could put on the left shoe without pulling her shoulder. The small request saved an ordinary motion rather than enlarging the task her present limbs could perform.

lark_e15_care_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_care_007.text: By the end of the second protected week, Lin could cross the room without rushing the turn. That visible change pleased her more than she expected. It still belonged to the current short ordinary walk; the outside stair and leg qi task had not been accepted. The next dated assessment would ask about those scopes separately. She wrote the completed ordinary distance and the fatigue afterward in her own patient note. When the record looked modest, she left it modest. A better ordinary step did not need to pretend it had already crossed the mountain.

lark_e15_duan_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_duan_001.text: Duan visited the lower room on Day One Hundred Six after his own accepted teaching at another table. The visit was ordinary company, not a tenth formal meeting taken from the course eighty. His cane remained beside the chair, and his swollen knee prevented an upper route he had once used without counting its landings. Lin offered him the stool she could now spare. He accepted it without making their two troublesome joints into a joke about who had paid more for wisdom. The room could contain a teacher's limitation and a student's at the same time.

lark_e15_duan_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_duan_002.text: He brought a badly drawn goose from one beginner's ordinary route exercise. The child had attached its feet to the wrong side and then explained that a clever goose might prefer to walk upside down. Lin said she admired the defense. Duan said so had he, but the next drawing still needed feet placed where an ordinary goose actually used them. He had permission to show this one unnamed example. They laughed at its invented gait without treating the laugh as evidence that her own clinical restrictions had become less serious since yesterday.

lark_e15_duan_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_duan_003.text: Lin asked whether the sixth primary pair would feel clearer than the fifth once she was ready. Duan said she could not buy that answer by imagining it. Its route had its own fixed references and ordinary task, and the current ankle made even discussing the lower limb practice feel too close to doing it prematurely. He would review the actual curriculum when the body and apparatus were ready. For now she could keep the named anatomy distinct on paper. Knowing what had not been practiced would keep the first later attempt from borrowing a result already earned elsewhere.

lark_e15_duan_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_duan_004.text: The two arm pairs and anterior and posterior lower limb pairs in her received fifth stage record remained the established four. The fifth proposed local route was a third upper limb primary pair; the sixth was the lateral lower limb primary pair. Both belonged to the bounded primary curriculum. Neither secretly crossed a governing or conception extraordinary bridge. Lin put the names on separate paper strips and stopped there. The effort involved ordinary reading, with no qi drawn into the ankle because a clear word on paper had made a future motion seem near.

lark_e15_duan_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_duan_005.text: Duan said his own six paired routes could be used on a best recovered day, and fewer when the knee swelled. The local six pair teaching scope came from that qualified experience. It did not require him to perform every route today to keep a student reassured. Lin had been glad to see his cane because it prevented her from making an imagined perfect teacher responsible for the mountain's damage. He said the cane was useful for walking, whether or not it improved her philosophy. She handed it back when the visit reached its ordinary end.

lark_e15_duan_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_duan_006.text: Before leaving, he asked what she had eaten. Lin described the provider's millet and greens with a seriousness that made him accuse her of reviewing a furnace. He had a neighbor who burned porridge regularly and called the dark layer evidence of courage. Lin said she would prefer a less courageous breakfast. Their conversation reached the door without settling any cultivation question. The next formal meeting remained a separately received appointment after present readiness, with its four copper due only for actual instruction. Today's company did not consume it.

lark_e15_story_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_story_001.text: Qin Yi returned the revised small bell drawing after school. Its rope now stopped below the figure's shoulder, and the bell looked so modest that Lin could scarcely distinguish it from the goat's paper shoe. The child said small did not mean unimportant. Lin agreed and asked what ordinary sound it made. Qin Yi produced a grunt that would have suited the turnip hound better. Shan Fang let her try again before asking whether the drawn bell might need its own sound rather than a familiar creature's. The page survived the disagreement without requiring another grown person to settle it.

lark_e15_story_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_story_002.text: The child asked Lin to add a story beside the drawing. Lin offered an account of the sorting reader who needed raised page corners, leaving his name and private folder out. Qin Yi wanted a villain flattening every corner in secret. Lin said she herself had proposed the change and had stopped when she learned what the corners did. That was less satisfying to the child, who preferred villains easy to identify. She agreed to draw a wrong corner if Lin would make its correction visible. They made the error large enough to be understood without turning its maker evil.

lark_e15_story_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_story_003.text: Shan Fang watched them argue over the drawer. She said her pupils often wanted a right answer to arrive with a face they could recognize forever afterward. A face made an error easier to remember and harder to revise. Lin had wanted the mountain inquiry to find one similarly convenient cause. The ordinary drawing gave her somewhere else to examine that desire. Its drawer had caught paper, its improver had asked a bad question, and its reader had corrected the method. No person had to become secretly malicious for the correction to matter.

lark_e15_story_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_story_004.text: The finished page stayed with Qin Yi under the family and lesson permission they had actually agreed. Lin kept no second private school collection merely because the drawing amused her. The child wanted to give Ke Wen the new bell page when his current visit scope allowed it. Shan would ask his receiver rather than surprise a recovering patient with a whole class. The waiting question disappointed her daughter for an hour. By supper she had invented a second ordinary sound for the tiny bell and was more interested in whether he would like it.

lark_e15_story_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_story_005.text: The ordinary household rhythms reached Lin through the open lower doorway: a pan set down, a child called away from gravel, a porter washing the new harness pad. She missed walking into those rhythms on her own chosen route. Visits were still scheduled around actual fatigue and patient room space. The quieter life was not an opportunity magically given in return for injury. It was a consequence she had to inhabit. She could enjoy the paper story and resent needing it to arrive at her chair. Neither feeling erased the ordinary help that had made the afternoon possible.

lark_e15_night_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_night_001.text: On the one hundred ninth evening, the crutch hire had reached its last day. Lin put its dated slip beside the morning assessment appointment. She would either return the support under a current accepted plan or ask for a real extension with a named price and source. The object could not become hers because she had become accustomed to it. She disliked the need to discuss another limit tomorrow, then found that writing the question made the morning less threatening.

lark_e15_night_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_night_002.text: The course notebook remained closed beneath the ordinary patient note. She had learned no sixth pair during these protected weeks. The fifth had not been made stable by letting time pass. Even the established four would need present permitted practice before an examination claimed what she could currently perform. The received stage record preserved what had been earned. It did not certify an injured evening's leg task. Lin set the paper strips beside it, where their anatomy would remain a beginning rather than evidence of completion.

lark_e15_night_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_night_003.text: Outside the shutter, the broken gallery's silhouette had changed where the qualified ground crew removed one loose piece. They had not reopened the upper route. The work made tomorrow's lower inspection possible inside a newly accepted scope. Lin listened to the ordinary cart returning tools and resisted going to the door merely to see its load. A present movement she could decline was easier to name than the absent paths she still wanted. She could let the cart finish without making herself its witness.

lark_e15_night_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e15_night_004.text: She finished the evening meal and checked the morning shoes for a folded lining. The ankle felt quiet while seated. She knew now that quiet at rest was one useful fact among several the ordinary examination would need. In the guide's room, an attendant lowered the lamp before the patient rested. No mountain light answered either of them. Lin put the next day's question beside the cup and went to sleep with its answer still belonging to a morning.
